topics.hook: $50 gone on every $200 booking.

topics.title: You don't need to quit Airbnb
topics.hook: You don't need to quit Airbnb.
topics.angle: Defuses the biggest objection before making the ask.

topics.title: $516 direct vs $312 via OTA
topics.hook: Same guest. Same room. Two very different outcomes.
topics.angle: Side-by-side seam; the cleanest single-image argument in the batch.

topics.title: 3 things every booking page needs to convert
topics.hook: A pretty site doesn't pay. A converting one does.
topics.angle: Bridges campaign and educational categories.

topics.title: Every month you wait, the middleman keeps his cut
topics.hook: This isn't a someday project. It's a meter running.
topics.angle: Cost of delay.

topics.title: 2 ways to go direct
topics.hook: A booking widget or a full integration.
topics.angle: Two doors, both open.

topics.title: Two ways to start
topics.hook: Both end the same way: your guests, your margin, your platform.
topics.angle: The offer post.

topics.title: The billboard effect: OTAs are your ad budget, not your enemy
topics.hook: Half the guests who find you on an OTA google you next.
topics.angle: The most credible, least preachy version of the whole argument — and it makes Kymbo look honest rather than anti-OTA. Strong candidate for the next batch.
proof: ~50% of OTA-discovered guests search the property directly before booking

topics.title: The 40–50% rule
topics.hook: You're not trying to hit 100% direct. You're trying to hit 45%.
topics.angle: Gives a target, which makes the project finite and non-threatening. Counter-intuitive for a company selling direct booking — which is exactly why it converts.
proof: 40–50% direct share is the independent-hotel sweet spot

topics.title: Rate parity doesn't forbid what you think it forbids
topics.hook: You can't undercut them. You can out-offer them.
topics.angle: Parity clauses restrict advertised *rate*, not *value*. Most owners think their hands are tied — they aren't.
proof: parity restricts public rate, not perks: breakfast, upgrade, flexible cancellation, early check-in, late checkout

topics.title: What you actually lose when Booking.com owns the email
topics.hook: They didn't take 18%. They took the guest.
topics.angle: Shifts the loss from money to asset. Sets up every CRM/loyalty argument that follows.
proof: direct booking connects the profile to CRM, loyalty, post-stay

topics.title: Cost per guest over three years, not one night
topics.hook: The commission isn't the price. It's the subscription.
topics.angle: Reframes commission as recurring cost of the same guest re-acquired. The strongest math angle not yet used.

topics.title: How many direct bookings pay for the whole system
topics.hook: Break-even is smaller than you think.
topics.angle: Removes the price objection with arithmetic instead of a discount.

topics.title: Overbooking costs more than commission
topics.hook: One walked guest wipes out a month of savings.
topics.angle: Connects the campaign to the technical category — the fix is a sync configuration.
proof: proper channel manager integration drops overbookings 90%+

topics.title: The upsells that only exist on your own checkout
topics.hook: Parking. Pets. Early check-in. The OTA sells none of them.
topics.angle: Direct isn't just cheaper, it has a bigger basket. Fresh angle — moves from cost-saving to revenue-adding.

topics.title: The post-stay email that books the second stay
topics.hook: The cheapest booking you'll ever get is the second one.
topics.angle: Makes the CRM layer tangible.

topics.title: Your OTA listing is your best ad. Use it like one.
topics.hook: Stop trying to leave. Start trying to convert.
topics.angle: Practical companion to fym-13 — what to actually change on the listing.

topics.title: Month one vs month twelve
topics.hook: What actually changes, and when.
topics.angle: Timeline post; sets honest expectations and handles the 'how long' objection.

topics.title: 'Commission-free' — read the contract
topics.hook: Free booking engine. Paid everything else.
topics.angle: Positions Kymbo as the straight-talker. Needs care: critique the practice, name no competitor.

topics.title: The cancellation policy is a conversion lever
topics.hook: Flexible on direct. Strict on OTA. Watch what happens.
topics.angle: A tactic they can run this week without touching their site — high practical value.
proof: free cancellation up to 48h is a legitimate parity-safe direct perk
